answer: Give each identity a lease that only survives a chain of linked tasks, each revealed only when the last is verified, arriving at unpredictable hours. Crossing that ridge alone is steady work; a grove of copies tended by one operator falls behind, because the queue branches faster than one mind can follow. Missed windows let leases lapse, and a jade-stamped renewal is earned only by the unbroken chain — so every extra copy shortens the life of all the rest.
